```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

office_lines <- read.csv("the-office_lines.csv")
```

1. The code below gives you a ranking of each character, calculating the length of lines for each character from The Office. I calculated the length of each line for each character and the summed up the length of all of their lines. 

```{r}
office_lines |>
  group_by(Character) |>
  mutate(line_length = str_length(Line))|>
  summarize(total_length = sum(line_length, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(total_length)) |>
  head(10)
```

2. One of the most common phrases that is repeated in The Office is "That's what she said." The main character Michael often repeats this innapropriate joke and I wanted to count how many times this joke was repeated by each character. First I found it helpful to change each string to all lower case and then use a regular expression brackets to choose either a straight or curly apostrophe. 

```{r}
office_lines |>
  mutate(Line = str_to_lower(Line))|>
  group_by(Character) |>
  summarize(exclaim_counter = sum(str_count(Line, "that['’]s what she said")))|>
  arrange(desc(exclaim_counter))
```


```{r}
office_lines |>
  mutate(new_company = str_replace_all(Line, "Dunder Mifflin", "Blunder Muffin")) |>
  filter(str_detect(new_company, "Blunder Muffin")) |>
  select(new_company) |> 
  head(2)
```
